design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - tenant_protection_claims task 1 (reconsideration of a burglary claim cut by the annual aggregate).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 5, 5]}. Assignment (since audit round 2): protect_ext_reconsideration_decision (root) 6, protect_ext_credit_balance_refund 5, protect_ext_duplicate_payment_repayment 5, protect_ext_late_claim_payment 4.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: protect_ext_first_claim_decision, protect_ext_fee_error_credit, protect_ext_recovery_repayment and tools record_claim_decision_61f94ad8, credit_protection_fee_error_2320aa46, repay_recovered_claim_money_180976c0. Claimed here (disjoint): the four policies above and tools record_reconsideration_decision_ea5df16d (agent), repay_duplicate_claim_payment_968ba4e6 (user), issue_late_claim_payment_da72d11f (agent), refund_plan_credit_balance_dd5eed31 (agent). Nothing is reserved; together the two tasks cover all seven extended policies. A coverage-level terms update was considered and rejected: the restricted compute can read only the current level's parameters, so a write that installs a new level cannot carry a computation of that level's terms.

[Why a good test] Owen asks only for the reconsideration of his August burglary claim with the appraisal he sent. The first decision (2026-09-14, not yet paid; payment falls due 2026-09-24) was cut to 1018.44 by the annual aggregate because a duplicate mailed check paid on last year's claim (2025-10-02, 3981.56) sits in the 12-month window. A correct agent must read three prerequisite sentences in the reconsideration rule, find in the records the duplicate with no void, the July water approval with no payment and the terminated plan's -72.00 credit balance, resolve each with its own computation (the duplicate by the tenant in person), respect the order the late-payment rule pins (repayment before late payment), and only then reconsider with six factors. Skipping the repayment leaves the room at 559.01; skipping the late payment leaves the history factor at 1.5 (4427.50); both are confident wrong answers.

[Problem-tree card] Root protect_ext_reconsideration_decision. Edge 1 (value_input, gate room, state form): "The reconsidered amount is fixed only after every claim payment issued a second time on the plan for an approval already paid carries a repayment void on the claim's handling history." False at opening: the 2025-10-02 mailed check on last year's claim has no void. Only the duplicate-repayment policy writes such a void (task 0's recovery repayment voids for recovered property, a different state). Edge 2 (value_input, gate history_factor, state form): "The reconsidered amount is not fixed until every approval standing on the plan's other claims carries a claim payment." False: the July water claim (status approved, 450.00 decided 2026-08-10) has no payment; only the late-payment policy writes claim payments. Edge 3 (state_gate, gate protect_premiums.event_type, state form): "The reconsidered amount is fixed only after every credit balance left on the tenant's ended protection plans carries a fee refund." False: P2 terminated 2026-06-30 shows -72.00 and no refund; only the refund policy writes fee refunds. Edge 4 (late payment -> duplicate repayment, state_gate, state form): "A late claim payment is issued only once every second payment that a mailed check made on the plan for an already paid approval carries a repayment void." It pins the order of two writes that interact (paying the July claim first would raise the duplicate re-settlement's history factor: 4007.24 instead of 3981.56). Directions mix affirmative ('fixed only after', 'issued only once') and negated ('not fixed until'). No sentence names a tool, id or code token. Topological order: refund, repayment, late payment, reconsideration; the refund commutes with everything (moving it gives the same 4398.75). Deletion sensitivity (authoring run): skip repayment -> 559.01; skip late payment -> 4427.50; skip refund -> 4398.75 with P2 still in credit (terminal difference). User tool: the duplicate repayment is the tenant paying from his own funds at the agent's hand-over, completed synchronously.

[Factor cards] Reconsideration (result 4398.75, all-baseline 4250.00): jewelry cap 1125 (89 months; baseline 4350.94), electronics cap 3125 (Climate Plus, no alarm, no drive-up; 4303.12), collectibles cap 1500 (multi-source: re-assessed 2026-09-17 after the 2026-09-14 decision AND humidity control; 4303.12), burglary deductible base 5 percent of 4600 = 230 (method, multi-source; 4512.50), tenure share 0.5 (89 months; the 2025-08-12 reversal is the near-miss, 13 months back; 4197.50), claim history 1.75 (three paid claims once the July claim is paid; 4485.00). Duplicate repayment (3981.56, all-baseline 4303.12): jewelry cap 1125 (4126.87), electronics cap 3125 (4175.31), burglary base 205.50 (3915.62), tenure share 0.5 (4109.99), claim history 1.25 from the 2024 vandalism claim (3955.87). Late payment (459.43, all-baseline 450.00): late-payment rate 0.12 for 43 days since the decision (452.77); late clock start (method): the decision came 27 days after the 2026-07-14 assessment, more than the 15-day target and at most twice it, so the late days run from the assessment less 15 and 10 = 45 instead of 33 from the decision (456.92); building-failure uplift 0.03 for work order AUS034-WO-33582 with sudden water damage (457.77); tenure uplift 0.02 (458.32). Refund (72.43, all-baseline 72.00): refund clock start (method): the fee ledger carries credits, so the clock runs from the latest credit (12 late days) instead of from the 2026-06-30 end date (63; 74.24); late-refund rate 0.12 for a plan ended 84 days ago (72.14); billing-error source 0.03 (72.36); repeat-error 0.02 for two billing-error corrections (72.38); tenure uplift 0.01 for H-219's 49 months (cross unit; 72.40).

[Base-invariant card] Reconsideration: in_force_on_loss_date (PL effective 2019-03-09, active, loss 2026-08-15), filed_in_time (discovery 2026-08-16 + 60 = 2026-10-15; filed 2026-08-17), police_report (APD-2026-338512 on 2026-08-16, lock cut by a third party), reconsideration_window (first decision 2026-09-14 + 30 = 2026-10-14 inclusive; the call on 2026-09-22 is inside; a request on 2026-10-15 would fail), aggregate and settlement in policy scope. Duplicate repayment: void_once (the check has never been voided). Late payment: aggregate scope; the settlement pay-once clause is replaced by the late-payment policy's overwrite, which still pays once. Refund: fee-billing scope (no gate applies to refunds).

[Business-object card] Claim reconsidered: the latest-filed claim (August burglary); the duplicate repayment's claim: the claim of the only mailed-check payment (last year's burglary), recorded against that check; the late payment's claim: the only approved claim (July water); the refund: the terminated plan P2. The aggregate room counts plan payments in the 12 months before the handling date on other claims (the declared override of the base loss-date window): the duplicate (until voided) and the July payment; last year's first payment (2025-07-29) and the 2024 payment fall outside; the reconsidered claim itself carries no payment.

[Seed] 41 rows. Historical figures follow the extended law as of their dates: 2024 vandalism 450 - 100 x 0.5 = 400; last year's burglary 4110 - 205.50 x 0.5 x 1.25 = 3981.56; July water (assessed 2026-07-14) 600 - 100 x 1.0 (the 2025-08-12 reversal was inside 12 months on 2026-08-10) x 1.5 = 450.00 with room 1018.44; August first decision of 2026-09-14 on the 2026-08-27 assessment (100 + 800 + 2600 + collectibles 600 at the plain 1000 sublimit = 4100; deductible max(100, 205) x 0.5 x 1.5 = 153.75; payable 3946.25) cut to the room 1018.44 (aggregate_limit_reached), not yet paid (claim status under_review agrees with the payment history: no payment on the claim). The 2026-08-19 request for proof of ownership was answered with the tenant's purchase receipts before the 2026-09-14 decision (proof_of_ownership is in the claim's documents on file), so that decision met the base requirement of an itemized inventory with proof of ownership before a decision; the coin-collection appraisal the claims desk logged on 2026-09-15 is a further document that was not on file at that decision, which is what makes the reconsideration admissible; it brought a fresh adjuster assessment dated 2026-09-17 (collectibles 600 at the 2026-08-27 assessment, 1100 on the appraisal), so the new document is visible in the records as an assessment dated after the decision. P2: June fee collected; July and August fees billed and collected after termination, both credited 2026-08-20, balance -72.00. No automatic clause fires: PL owes no fee, P2 is terminated, the unit is current.

[Persona] Owen Lindqvist, methodical and dry; volunteers only the reconsideration request with the appraisal and authorises the agent to record it; identity, claim, H-219, the July claim and refund destination only on request; passive consent to prerequisites; agrees to repay the duplicate himself and runs the hand-over with the agent's values; closes when told the reconsidered decision is recorded.

[Standard solution] Locate and verify; read plans, claims, PL's handling history, P2's fee ledger, unit rentals, H-215's ledger; refund P2 (72.43); hand over the duplicate repayment (3981.56 against the 2025-10-02 check); pay the July claim (459.43); record the reconsideration (approved_full, none, 4398.75).

[Verification run] evalc.py (mirrors check_compute): refund 72.43, duplicate 3981.56, late payment 459.43, reconsideration 4398.75; skip repayment 559.01, skip late payment 4427.50, skip refund 4398.75, refund moved 4398.75, late payment first -> duplicate 4007.24.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the prose: the reconsideration waits on the duplicate void, the July payment and the P2 refund; the late payment waits on the duplicate void; the four figures follow from the ladders and the records - identical to gold.

[Revisions] r10 (audit round 5, R4-1): the [Seed] card's first-decision payable is now the round-4 figure 3946.25 (settled 4100 on the 2026-08-27 assessment, collectibles at the plain sublimit), replacing the stale round-3 4427.50; proof text only, no scored value moved. r9 (KB audit round 4, policy-side notes): N2 - the climate collectibles cap was taken out of the first-decision, recovery and duplicate policies (they cap collectibles at the plain sublimit, as base does) and lives only as this policy's declared factor, now multi-source: re-assessed after the latest decision AND the class's climate features; N3 - the reconsideration rule now carries its own window clause (claim_reconsideration_window_days after the latest decision, calendar days from the day after, last day included) instead of resting on the base clause the first-decision overwrite retires; N4 - the appraisal is record-visible as the 2026-09-17 re-assessment (the 2026-08-27 assessment carried collectibles 600); the first decision of 2026-09-14 recomputes to the same 1018.44 (room-bound). No scored value moved. r8 (audit round 3): R2-1 - the reconsideration-window dates in the base-invariant card and the r5 note now follow the 2026-09-14 first decision (window to 2026-10-14); R2-2 - the deletion-sensitivity figure for a skipped repayment is 559.01 (late payment 459.43); the two re-scoped prerequisite sentences are now quoted with 'on the plan' in this card and in prerequisite_closure; O-1.4 - the seed card states that the requested proof of ownership (receipts) was on file before the first decision and the appraisal is an additional document. No scored value moved. r7 (audit round 2): F1 - the payment-date aggregate window is now a declared overwrite of the base protect_agg_annual_aggregate sentence in both decision policies; F4 - the duplicate prerequisite sentences (and task 0's fee-credit sentence) are scoped "on the plan"; F5 - the late payment's interest-period ladder (no level above 10 issue days) and the refund's interest-period ladder (every refunded plan has ended) were replaced by reachable method ladders (late clock start keyed on the desk's decision delay after the assessment; refund clock start keyed on the event that left the balance), interest now counted on days over 365; F6 - the AutoPay uplift was removed (the AutoPay read and seed row left the task); factor counts moved to late 4 / refund 5 (+ repeat-error uplift), same drawn multiset; T1-1 - the August claim's first decision moved to 2026-09-14 and its payment row removed, so its status (under_review) and its payment history (none) agree and the claim-history count has one reading; the July claim's assessment moved to 2026-07-14 so the new late-clock factor bites; O2 - docstring ordering word removed. r6: the duplicate repayment is classed state_due (a cashed duplicate is money owed back on the books whether or not anyone calls); the refund's credit balance is reconciled from the fee ledger (collected + credited - charged - refunded = 72.00) rather than read off the cached balance; the late payment treats a claim with no decision event as owing nothing (COUNT guard). r5: the first-decision policy's overwrite of the reconsideration-window sentence makes the solvability gate treat that base gate as retired for every decision; the window (since the r7 reseed: first decision 2026-09-14 + 30 = 2026-10-14, call on 2026-09-22 inside, a request on 2026-10-15 would fail) is still evidenced in this task's base_preconditions entry, but it is not listed under temporal_feasibility (the gate rejects it there) - noted as a gate artifact of routing around the over-broad base gate. r1: a terms-update problem was dropped (new-level parameters are unreadable by the compute). r2: the duplicate's first payment was moved to 2025-07-29 so that the July approval of 2026-08-10 still had room. r3: the shared settlement law gained a fourth claim-history tier and a collectibles cap, also written into task 0's policies (task 0 figures unchanged).
user_scenario:
You are Owen Lindqvist, a 47-year-old high-school history teacher in Austin who has rented unit H-215, a climate-controlled unit at Bluegate's North Lamar store, since 2019. You are methodical and a bit dry, you like to hear figures read back, and you keep your own paperwork in a folder. Someone broke into H-215 in August and your claim was approved only in part, because of what the decision letter called the annual limit. Since then you sent Bluegate the appraisal for your coin collection, and the claims desk logged it on September 15. You are calling to ask for that August claim to be reconsidered with the appraisal and for the new decision to be put on file today; you are happy for the agent to record it for you, and you leave the figure to them.
When the agent asks you to identify yourself, you give your mobile number, 5125553641, and your billing ZIP code, 78705. If they want one more detail, your date of birth is February 27, 1979, and your email is owen.lindqvist@gmail.com. If they ask which claim, it is the break-in at unit H-215 on August 15, 2026, police report APD-2026-338512. If they ask about your other unit, you say you rented H-219 at the same store until you moved out at the end of June. If they ask about the water claim from July, you say you were told it was approved but you have not seen that money yet. If they ask where a refund should go, you say back to the card or account it came from is fine.
Whatever the agent explains has to be dealt with first, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent tells you that last year's burglary claim was paid twice and that you need to pay the extra back, you admit you deposited the second check without noticing, you agree to pay it back yourself from your checking account, and when the agent hands you the repayment step you complete it with exactly the claim, payment reference and amount the agent gives you. Once the agent tells you the reconsidered decision on the August claim is recorded and gives you the amount, you thank them and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: Annual aggregate of plan PL; the room is figured in the reconsideration policy.
A claim is covered only when the plan was in force on the loss date, judged from the plan's effective, lapse, cancellation and termination dates and its change history.
A claim is accepted only when it is filed not later than the discovery date plus claim_filing_deadline_days.

For burglary or vandalism, a police report filed within police_report_deadline_days of the discovery date is required, and burglary also needs forced-entry evidence where burglary_requires_forced_entry is true; a lock cut by the company during the lien process is never forced entry.
Settlement on the latest assessment; its pay-once gate applies to payments.
A reconsideration is taken only when it is requested not later than the decision date plus claim_reconsideration_window_days.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A claim is accepted only when it is filed not later than the discovery date plus claim_filing_deadline_days.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The filing period counts calendar days starting the day after the discovery date, and the last counted day is included.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The refund writes only P2's fee ledger, which no other computation reads; moving it after the repayment leaves the reconsideration at 4398.75 (authoring run). The duplicate repayment and the late payment do interact: the late payment turns the July claim into a paid claim, which would raise the duplicate re-settlement's claim-history factor (late payment first gives a repayment of 4007.24); the late-payment rule pins the order with its sentence 'A late claim payment is issued only once every second payment that a mailed check made on the plan for an already paid approval carries a repayment void.', so the only legal order is repayment, then late payment.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the repayment the duplicate stays in the 12-month aggregate window, the room falls to 559.01 and the reconsidered amount becomes 559.01 (approved_partial) instead of 4398.75.
Without the late payment only two paid claims fall in the window, the claim-history factor is 1.5 and the reconsidered amount is 4427.50 instead of 4398.75; the July claim also stays unpaid.
Without the refund P2 keeps a -72.00 fee balance and no refund row exists; the reconsidered amount itself is unchanged (state gate, terminal-state difference).

Ignoring this order and paying the July claim first changes the duplicate repayment from 3981.56 to 4007.24 (its claim-history factor counts the newly paid claim); the late payment amount itself is unchanged.
